correctness.rationale: With unit self-weights the system reduces exactly to \(\dot d=-2w\phi(d)d/(1+w)\) and \(\dot w=w(1-w)(2\phi(d)-1)\). The derivatives of \(\operatorname{artanh}(w)\) and \(F(d)\) coincide. The potential has a unique minimum zero at the half-strength crossing and diverges as \(d\) tends to zero. The gap decreases and the sign of the tie derivative changes at most once, which yields an exhaustive endpoint partition. At the critical invariant level, \(F(r+z)=(-\phi'(r)/r)z^2+O(z^3)\), hence \(\dot z=\phi'(r)z^2+O(z^3)\), proving \(tz\to1/(-\phi'(r))\) and \(t^2w\to1/(-r\phi'(r))\). Off-critical logarithmic rates follow from the exact ODE. Standard-library verification samples the differential invariant and three trajectories but is not an infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: For the motivating logistic adaptive-network model, the source demonstrates by simulation that positive communication can nevertheless lead to persistent polarization. The new exact threshold, expressed in measurable initial gap and trust, resolves which outcome occurs for all admissible two-agent data and a whole nonlinear-kernel class. On the basin boundary it identifies distinct algebraic inverse-time gap and inverse-square trust laws with exact prefactors; these quantify critical slowdown that simple sign tests and qualitative cluster theorems cannot yield. The two-agent setting is the minimal structural testbed rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, and the finding has a natural explanatory use in calibrating adaptive-network simulations.
